subject: chemistry
title: Group 1 and Group 7
welcome_lead: Meet the soft fizzing metals and the colourful biting non-metals.
meta_desc: Explore alkali metals and halogens in this KS3 chemistry adventure on the periodic table.
final_note: You can now spot the highly reactive elements at the edges of the table.

concepts.def: Soft, reactive metals that fizz in water.
Group 1 gets MORE reactive going DOWN.
Group 7 gets LESS reactive going DOWN.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Group 1 contains lithium, sodium, potassium and more. They are soft enough to cut with a knife and react vigorously with water to make an alkali solution and hydrogen gas.

Reactivity increases going DOWN the group.

Group 7 contains fluorine, chlorine, bromine, iodine. They are coloured non-metals: F is pale yellow gas, Cl is green gas, Br is red-brown liquid, I is dark grey solid.

Reactivity decreases going DOWN the group.

Elements in the same group behave similarly because they have the same number of outer electrons.

Same group = same chemistry.

mcqs.q: Why does water have a bent shape rather than linear?
options: Water is bent because oxygen is heavier than hydrogen and weighs the middle down.
Entropy measures how much energy a system contains in total.
Oxygen has two bonding pairs and two lone pairs, giving a tetrahedral electron geometry but a bent molecular shape.
Water is bent because the hydrogens repel each other and push apart.

mcqs.q: What does an increase in entropy of a system correspond to?
options: Entropy measures how much energy a system contains in total.
An increase in the number of ways energy and particles can be arranged — typically a more dispersed/'disordered' state.
Heterogeneous catalysts are consumed; homogeneous catalysts are not.
Entropy is just a measure of how messy a system looks visually.

mcqs.q: What distinguishes a heterogeneous from a homogeneous catalyst?
options: Heterogeneous catalysts are solid and homogeneous catalysts are liquid — full stop.
A heterogeneous catalyst is in a different phase from the reactants; a homogeneous catalyst is in the same phase.
Entropy measures how much energy a system contains in total.
Heterogeneous catalysts are consumed; homogeneous catalysts are not.
